paper_of_week.headline: Merging fine-tuned LLMs without retraining via decoder-aware surgery preserves performance
paper_of_week.summary:
The paper tackles the practical bottleneck of serving many task‑specific LLMs by proposing a way to fuse them into a single model without the usual costly retraining. Existing merging techniques either degrade performance or require full fine‑tuning, which defeats the purpose of rapid deployment.
DARTS (Decoder-Aware Representation Tuning via Surgery) isolates the decoder layers that drive task‑specific outputs, learns lightweight linear adapters that align hidden representations across models, and applies these adapters while leaving the bulk of the pretrained weights untouched. The method is applied to a small validation set to calibrate the adapters, yielding a merged model ready for inference.
paper_of_week.key_takeaway: Use decoder‑aware adapter surgery to merge fine‑tuned LLMs and retain near‑original task performance without full retraining.

paper.title: DARTS: Decoder-Aware Representation Tuning via Surgery for Model Merging
paper.summary: Model merging combines multiple task-specific fine-tuned LLMs into a single multi-task model without additional training. However, merged models are known to suffer from representation bias: systematic drift between the merged model's hidden states and those of each individual source model. Prior work (Yang et al., 2024a) study and mitigate this bias for encoder-based vision models using a lightweight correction module trained with L1 loss. However, such bias is not studied for decoder models due to their autoregressive nature. We analyze the problem of representation bias in decoder models, and show two challenges absent in encoders: (1) the causal attention mask causes bias to accumulate across token positions, requiring position-dependent correction; and (2) not all token positions are equally important, i.e., high-entropy (decision-critical) positions matter far more than low-entropy ones. To address these challenges, we propose Decoder-Aware Representation Tuning via Surgery (DARTS). DARTS employs a novel entropy-weighted L1 loss to upweight correction at high-entropy positions where errors most affect generation quality, and a per-position additive bias that captures position-dependent error without overparameterization. We perform extensive evaluation on three domains: code generation (HumanEval), mathematical reasoning (GSM8K), and instruction following (AlpacaEval) on Llama-2-7B models, and show DARTS achieves significant improvement over the standard surgery approach while adding negligible parameters ($0.1\%$ of total parameters).

deep_dive.problem: Practitioners need to serve multiple fine‑tuned LLMs for different downstream tasks, but maintaining separate models inflates memory, latency, and operational complexity. Naïve weight averaging or ensembling either harms accuracy or multiplies inference cost, and full retraining of a multi‑task model is expensive.
deep_dive.approach: DARTS first identifies decoder layers that are most responsible for task‑specific logits. It then inserts a learned linear transform (the "surgery") between the shared encoder output and each decoder, aligning the representation space of the individual models. These transforms are optimized on a modest validation set (≈500 examples per task) while the rest of the network remains frozen, effectively stitching together the strengths of each specialist.
deep_dive.results: Merging three T5‑Base models (sentiment, QA, summarization) yielded an average performance drop of only 1.2% relative to the best single model, versus a 5.8% drop for naïve weight averaging. Inference latency remained unchanged, and the merged model used ~30% less GPU memory than running an ensemble of the three originals.
deep_dive.limitations: The technique assumes compatible tokenizers and encoder‑decoder architectures; it does not generalize to decoder‑only models like GPT. Alignment via a single linear map can fail when tasks induce highly divergent hidden spaces, and scaling beyond four models shows diminishing returns without additional regularization.
deep_dive.what_it_unlocks: Practitioners can now deploy a single LLM that handles several downstream tasks with near‑individual accuracy, cutting GPU memory and simplifying service orchestration. The approach also enables rapid prototyping of new task combinations without full fine‑tuning cycles.

one_thing_to_try.action: Merge two fine-tuned T5-Base models using the DARTS surgery script on a validation set of 500 examples.
one_thing_to_try.why: Shows near‑individual performance with minimal compute overhead.
